on 3 November, 2025
 The Honourable Smt.Justice Tirumala Devi Eada
 Criminal Petition No.9389 of 2025
Order:

This Criminal Petition is filed by the petitioners-accused Nos.1 to 7 seeking to quash the proceedings in SC No.857 of 2023 on the file of XVI Special Sessions Judge FTC for Atrocities against Women to Hyderabad, for the offences under Sections 376, 366, 354B, 354C, 384, 385, 493 read with 120-B IPC and Section 67-A of the Information Technology Act (for short 'IT Act').

entities.label: COURT

sentences.text: 2. Heard Sri Rama Rao Immaneni, learned counsel for the petitioners and Sri Jithender Rao Veeramalla, learned Additional Public Prosecutor for the respondent No.1-State.

3. Learned counsel for the petitioners has submitted that the petitioner No.1 married the respondent No.3 against the will and wish of respondent No.2, father of respondent No.3, and that is the reason,
respondent No.2 has been filing several cases against the petitioner No.1 and his family members.

The respondent No.2 and his wife have filed a Writ of Habeas Corpus vide WP No.46786 of 2022 before this Court alleging that respondent No.3 went missing and sought a direction against the petitioners herein to produce her.

The said writ petition was dismissed as the respondent No.3 herself ETD,J appeared before the court and she was examined by a Division Bench of this Court and she stated that she has married the petitioner No.1 according to her own will and wish and without there being any coercion.

The learned counsel for the petitioners also submitted that earlier when petitioner No.1 and the respondent No.3 were leading their family life at Gujarat, the father of the victim has brought the victim back, pursuant to which the husband of the victim i.e. petitioner No.1 herein has filed a writ petition before the High Court of Gujarat, wherein again she submitted a declaration stating that she wanted to live with her husband.

Now, in the present petition, the respondent No.2 has filed a complaint against the petitioners for the offences under Sections 376,
366, 354B, 354C, 384, 385, 493 read with 120-B IPC and Section 67-A of the IT Act.

4. Learned counsel for the petitioners further submitted that since both the petitioner No.1 and respondent No.3 are happily married and leading a family life, the compliant has no merits and none of the ingredients attract the offences alleged against the petitioner No.1 and his family members.
He, therefore, prayed to quash the proceedings.
ETD,J 5.

Learned counsel for the respondent No.3 has submitted that the respondent No.3 is very much into happy married life with the petitioner No.1 and that they are blessed with a baby boy on 17.07.2024 at GMERS General Hospital, Gandhi Nagar and the said birth certificate of the child is also filed along with the petition.

It is only the respondent No.2, who is creating problems in the Soniwala Musaddiq Mohammed Yusuf vs The State Of Telangana on 3 November, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/30550881/
1 marital life of the petitioner No.1 and the respondent No.3 and that they are being disturbed by the complaints filed by the respondent No.2.

sentences.text:
6. Perused the record.
7.
A perusal of the order in WP No.46786 of 2022 discloses the fact that respondent No.3 appeared before the Division Bench and stated that she married the petitioner No.1 willfully.
Further the marriage certificate and the birth certificate of the child of petitioner No.1 and the respondent No.3 are also perused.

Thus, in the facts and circumstances of the case, since the petitioner No.1 and the respondent No.3 are already married and are leading a peaceful married life, continuation of proceedings against the petitioner No.1 and his family members would be an abuse of process of law.

8. Accordingly, the Criminal Petition is allowed and the proceedings against the petitioners-accused Nos.1 to 7 in SC ETD,J No.857 of 2023 on the file of XVI Special Sessions Judge FTC for Atrocities against Women to Hyderabad, are hereby quashed.
